sections.what_happened: In the hours before US midterm polls opened Tuesday, federal judges restricted the Trump administration's efforts to pressure state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting: one Washington judge blocked demands that California not count ballots from people on an alleged-noncitizen list; another barred sending such lists to officials in any state; the 9th Circuit upheld an order stopping threats of prosecution against election officials. This followed the Supreme Court swiftly rejecting the administration's request to intervene in a Justice Department suit seeking to set aside California mail ballots from 20,000+ people it said may be noncitizens. Judges found the lists inaccurate and risking disenfranchisement of naturalized citizens.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) wire reporting; no second publisher family verified in-window for the same rulings (The Hindu liveblog covered the Supreme Court rejection in substance but was not separately verified as a family for this item).
sections.what_disputed: The administration's position (noncitizen voting crackdown as election integrity) is reported in the same piece; no ruling on the merits of any individual voter's status was made -- the orders concern lists, counting and threats, not final eligibility findings.
